This check makes four record checks and each was watched failing on its own, because an xUnit test stops at the first assertion that fires: a mutation that trips an earlier one proves nothing about a later one. The four, in the order the test makes them, with the error message each printed. (Four scope guards stand ahead of them, so that a census looking at nothing cannot pass — that `OperationEvaluatorTests`, `DeterminismTests` and `WeatherMinimumsMetEntryPointTests` are each inside what was counted, and that the generated-class harvest returned something. Those are the three classes `RecordedMutationTests` names, not the three this file names: the third is an entry-point test filed under `weather-minimums-met` in the overlay, and this file does not name it at all. None of those four guards has been watched, and docs/decisions/0007 says so and says what would fire each.) **(1) Nothing runs unnamed.** One row of this file stopped naming a test that runs (`"test": "DeterminismTests.The_same_request_resolves_the_same_way_every_time_but_not_under_this_name"` for `"test": "DeterminismTests.The_same_request_resolves_the_same_way_every_time"`), so that test ran with no record -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   683, Skipped:     0, Total:   684` on both net8.0 and net10.0, and nothing else in the suite went red, on `these tests run and no record names the mutation that reddens them, so nobody has watched them fail (AGENTS.md §7). A test that proves one map entry's rule belongs in that entry's `tests` in corpus-map.overlay.json; one that proves something no single entry owns belongs in tests/FaaPart107.Tests/cross-cutting-mutations.json (docs/decisions/0007): DeterminismTests.The_same_request_resolves_the_same_way_every_time`. **(2) Nothing is named that does not run.** A row naming a method no class declares was ADDED to this file (`"test": "DeterminismTests.A_test_this_engine_does_not_have"`) rather than an existing row being renamed, which is what makes this the second assertion's mutation and not the first's again: every test that runs is still named, so assertion 1 passes and the record's claim to evidence for a test that does not exist is what fires -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   683, Skipped:     0, Total:   684` on both net8.0 and net10.0, and nothing else in the suite went red, on `cross-cutting-mutations.json names tests that no longer exist: DeterminismTests.A_test_this_engine_does_not_have`. **(3) One record each.** A cross-cutting row was copied into an entry's `tests` in `corpus-map.overlay.json` (`DeterminismTests.The_same_request_resolves_the_same_way_every_time` added under `speed-within-limit`), so two records named one test and could disagree about it -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   683, Skipped:     0, Total:   684` on both net8.0 and net10.0, and nothing else in the suite went red, on `these tests are named by an entry's overlay row and by cross-cutting-mutations.json, so two records can disagree about one test: DeterminismTests.The_same_request_resolves_the_same_way_every_time`. **(4) No row is empty of a mutation.** One `mutation` string was blanked (the `The_evaluation_does_not_collapse_to_a_boolean_and_offers_no_way_to_claim_one` row's, `""` for its text) -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   683, Skipped:     0, Total:   684` on both net8.0 and net10.0, and nothing else in the suite went red, on `these cross-cutting rows record no mutation, and a test nobody has seen go red is not evidence: OperationEvaluatorTests.The_evaluation_does_not_collapse_to_a_boolean_and_offers_no_way_to_claim_one`. Each mutation was applied to the committed tree, built, run over the whole suite on both target frameworks, and reverted, with `git status --porcelain` clean afterwards. That is this check failing on each of the conditions it exists for, observed rather than asserted (issue #98's criterion 3).

One gated entry's handler -- `operating-limitations`' -- demanded its typed input ahead of the rule's § 107.205 gate -- the ordering thirteen of the fifteen gated entries took before #93 -- by wrapping the argument back up (`Demand(request.Person, request.EntryId, nameof(request.Person))` for `request.Person`). A caller stating a certificate of waiver of § 107.51 in force and describing nothing else was then refused `ArgumentException` naming `Person` -- `FactRequired`, `MissingInput=Person`, filed under `Outstanding`, which `OperationEvaluation.Outstanding` documents as "everything the caller still owes this engine" -- instead of being declined `OutsideCurrentScope` citing § 107.205 (`docs/decisions/0008-the-waiver-gate-precedes-every-other-demand.md`). So this test, which pins no suspended entry filed under what the caller still owes, went red on both target frameworks: `Failed!  - Failed:     4, Passed:   739, Skipped:     0, Total:   743` for net10.0 and the same figures for net8.0. The others red with it were `WaiverGateOrderingTests.A_waived_request_that_describes_nothing_else_is_declined_OutsideCurrentScope_citing_107_205`; `WaiverGateOrderingTests.A_waived_request_is_never_asked_for_a_typed_input_the_waiver_has_made_irrelevant`; `OperatingLimitationsEntryPointTests.The_dictionary_dispatch_refuses_rather_than_answering_from_defaults`. Filed here rather than under `operating-limitations`: the test waives every gated regulation at once and asserts with `Assert.All` over all twenty-seven suspended entries, so it is a census that belongs to no single entry, and filing it under one would make that entry's packet claim evidence it does not have (`docs/decisions/0007-a-test-that-belongs-to-no-entry-records-its-mutation-beside-the-tests.md`). Any one of the fifteen handler mutations recorded in the overlay reddens it; this is the one that was observed for this row.

This test compares the table with the generated request types by reflection, and went red naming the missing one on both target frameworks: `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   741, Skipped:     0, Total:   742` for net10.0 and the same figures for net8.0, on `Assert.Equal() Failure: Collections differ`, `Expected: [..., "WellClearRequest"]` against `Actual: [...]` without it -- this test ALONE in the whole suite, which is the point: nothing else notices a gated entry that the table forgot.
